version.changelog: 模块化重构：拆分browser/extractor/formatter/validator，新增commander命令行支持

llm.summary: This skill mostly does what it claims, but it needs review because weak URL checks can let a supplied link make the local browser visit unintended sites or private network addresses.

dimensions.detail: Launching local headless Chromium is proportionate for rendered WeChat pages, but without hostname, redirect, or private-address controls it can make network requests from the user's environment beyond the disclosed WeChat article use case.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses npm plus Playwright Chromium installation. The package declares Playwright and Commander, while the documentation also says there are no third-party dependencies; the lockfile resolves packages from a third-party registry mirror and install commands are not fully pinned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documented scope is mp.weixin.qq.com article links, but validation only checks for substrings and then passes the URL to page.goto, so crafted URLs or redirects can leave the intended host scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact-backed evidence of credential use, persistent browser profiles, filesystem storage of fetched content, startup hooks, services, or cross-session persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to fetch WeChat Official Account article title, body text, and final URL using Playwright, and the main script implements that flow with validation, browser navigation, extraction, and formatting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing in environments with private services or sensitive network access. Use only trusted WeChat article URLs, avoid running it on untrusted links, and prefer pinned dependency installation from a registry you trust. Also use fetched article content only where you have permission to archive or repurpose it.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: validator.js uses substring checks for mp.weixin.qq.com and /s/, and wx-article-fetch.js sends the accepted value directly to Playwright navigation without redirect or request-scope enforcement.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a supply-chain note: package-lock.json uses registry.npmmirror.com for dependencies with integrity hashes, which is not evidence of active compromise but adds an avoidable third-party distribution dependency.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the full artifact does include browser automation and extraction in wx-article-fetch.js, browser.js, extractor.js, validator.js, and formatter.js, so the claimed implementation mismatch is not supported by the complete package.
[P1] expected: Downgraded: the cited text is a normal CLI '--debug' option description and not an instruction to override agent or system behavior.
[RP1] expected: Partially accepted as install hygiene: using npx playwright install chromium is expected for this Playwright-based skill, but the documentation should pin versions or prefer deterministic npm ci workflows.
[SC1] expected: Partially accepted as install hygiene: package.json uses semver ranges for direct dependencies while the lockfile pins resolved versions; this is not hidden behavior but users should treat dependency updates as code changes.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as user guidance rather than a security verdict driver: archiving, research, and repurposing article text match the tool purpose but should be used only where permitted by rights and platform terms.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese comments are coherent with a WeChat-specific tool, and the primary README and SKILL documentation are bilingual enough to understand the runtime behavior.
